title: Browsers & ChromeOS — Threat Intelligence Update
headline: Public PoC code is now listed for CVE-2026-74936, a WebAssembly use-after-free in Firefox and Thunderbird that Mozilla fixed in August. Google also shipped a ChromeOS / ChromeOS Flex stable update covering about 404 CVEs. Neither source marks any flaw as exploited.
summary: AEGIS lists a first public GitHub PoC (SneakyNachos/CVE-2026-74936-gc-potato) for CVE-2026-74936. The flaw was fixed on 2026-08-18 in Firefox 154, ESR 140.14 and ESR 153.1, and in Thunderbird 154, 140.14 and 153.1 (Mozilla MFSA 2026-74, impact high). NVD scores it 9.8, while Red Hat scores it 7.5 because exploitation requires user interaction. Hosts still on older builds are at risk. Google also published a Stable Channel Update for ChromeOS / ChromeOS Flex on 2026-11-23 (16868.29.0, Chrome 158.0.8127.98). AEGIS links about 404 CVEs to it. In a sample of the linked CVEs, none is KEV-listed or marked exploited.
changes: 2026-08-18: Mozilla fixed CVE-2026-74936 in Firefox 154 and the ESR and Thunderbird releases (MFSA 2026-74).
2026-11-23: Google published the ChromeOS / ChromeOS Flex stable update 16868.29.0 (Chrome Releases). AEGIS ingested it on 2026-11-27 (alert 3e912eb75903).
2026-11-27: a public PoC was listed for CVE-2026-74936 (AEGIS alert c90fc7b48c40).
assessment: CVE-2026-74936: NVD 9.8; Red Hat 7.5 (AV:N/AC:H/UI:R). Mozilla impact: high. ChromeOS update: about 404 CVEs of mixed severity.
Network. The victim must load malicious web or mail content, and no authentication is needed.
Memory corruption in the JavaScript/WebAssembly engine, a potential code execution path inside the content process.
None reported (Mozilla, Red Hat, Tenable; AEGIS).
CVE-2026-74936: 1 GitHub repository, unvetted (AEGIS). ChromeOS: none flagged.
Patches have been available since August 2026 for Firefox and Thunderbird, and since 2026-11-23 for ChromeOS. Priority: verify version compliance.
affected: Drive-by memory corruption on user endpoints
Malicious content rendered in the mail client
Multiple browser and OS flaws on managed Chromebooks
actions: Confirm Firefox and Thunderbird fleets, including ESR and Linux distribution packages, are at or above the fixed versions. Remediate stragglers.
Confirm managed ChromeOS devices have received 16868.29.0 or later through the admin console.
Response targets are AEGIS recommendations, not mandatory CISA deadlines.
monitoring: Mozilla and Chrome follow regular release trains; the next Chrome stable desktop release, 159, is in early stable.
limitations: The PoC has not been validated. The ChromeOS post's full CVE list and severities were not reviewed individually, and only a sample of the linked CVEs was checked against AEGIS exploitation data. Google's text did not confirm the seven ChromeOS-specific fixes reported by Chrome Unboxed.
judgment: Confirmed: public PoC code is listed for an older Firefox and Thunderbird flaw that was patched in August, and a large routine ChromeOS update has shipped. Neither involves reported exploitation. The practical risk falls on unmanaged or lagging installations. This is a version-compliance check, not an emergency.
